column2: re-entry admission claims (admit() claims the requested slot before the eviction callbacks; victims must be RESIDENT)
column5: master livelock in admit() through the public API (P1 HANG.txt); the selector-only fix publishes the admitted slot twice (P1 VARIANTS.tsv), so the claim is part of the atom; no owner contract or commit chose otherwise: the atom was received by M3JDK in 452b77db672 and lost by the retain merge 7c6ddb6b7aa (PR #2157: "Promotion to live code is a reviewed follow-up")

column2: callback Error restoration (an Error from factory/read/decode/spill-delete or encode/write restores the slot's prior state)
column5: master restores the state on IOException/RuntimeException/Exception but not on Error, so an AssertionError/LinkageError/OutOfMemoryError from a callback leaves CREATING, RESTORING or SWAPPING for good and the slot refuses every later call with "reentrant residency transition" (the 7 tests fail on master with exactly those states); the owner's own catch blocks show the intent (restore, then rethrow the original); nothing in the owner's Javadoc, tests or history keeps a slot transitional after an Error; same lost atom (crate step m3-doop-callback-error-20261030, in 452b77db672); STUCK_STATE.txt: on master one Error from Codec.encode makes the next over-budget admission livelock (a second public-API livelock, no re-entry needed); with P1 alone the SWAPPING slot stays counted, unevictable and refused for good; with leaf A it is RESIDENT again and the next admission swaps it
